title: Going to: vou falar
description: Talk about plans with ir + infinitive, the everyday future in Brazil.

guide.summary: The everyday way to talk about the future in Brazil is ir in the present plus an infinitive: vou falar, I am going to speak. Learn four forms of ir and you can make plans for anyone.

sections.title: Four forms of ir
sections.text: Conjugate ir in the present for the person, then add the second verb in the infinitive. Você, ele, ela and a gente share one form; vocês, eles and elas share another.
steps: Find the subject.
Take its form of ir from the table.
Add the second verb in the infinitive.

examples.en: I am going to buy bread.
They are going to have dinner at home.

watch: A gente means we but takes vai, not vamos.
Vais goes with tu; with você always use vai.

sections.title: The second verb never changes
sections.text: Ir already shows who and when, so the verb after it stays in its dictionary form, ending in -ar, -er or -ir.
steps: Conjugate only ir.
Write the second verb exactly as in the dictionary.
Check it ends in -r.

examples.pt: Nós vamos jogar futebol no sábado.
examples.en: We are going to play football on Saturday.
She is going to buy a car.

watch: Vamos estudamos marks the person twice: only ir changes.

sections.title: Saying not: não vou
sections.text: Não goes right before the form of ir, never between ir and the infinitive.
steps: Find the form of ir.
Put não directly in front of it.
Leave the infinitive where it was.

examples.en: I am not going to work tomorrow.
We are not going to watch TV.

watch: Vou não comer is wrong: não comes first.
In speech you may hear a second não at the end: não vou, não. The first one is still required.

sections.title: Words for when
sections.text: Plans come with future time words. They usually go at the start or at the end of the sentence.
steps: Check the time word points forward.
Days take no (or na) before them: no sábado.
Put the time word first or last.

examples.pt: Na semana que vem vou viajar.
examples.en: Next week I am going to travel.
I am going to study on Saturday.

watch: Ontem and na semana passada are past: they cannot go with a plan.
In speech the no is often dropped: vou estudar sábado.

sections.title: Going somewhere: vou para a praia
sections.text: To say you are going to a place, use ir once, then para (or a) and the place with its article. Vou ir is heard in casual speech, but careful Portuguese uses ir once: vou already means I am going.
steps: Use one form of ir only.
Add para, then the article and the place.
À or ao (a + article) is also right and a bit more formal.

examples.pt: No sábado vou para a praia.
examples.en: On Saturday I am going to the beach.
We are going to the market.

watch: Vou ir para a praia doubles the verb.
Vou na praia is common in casual speech, but para a is the safe form.

sections.title: Pronouns: vou te ligar
sections.text: An object pronoun like me or te goes between the form of ir and the infinitive. This is the natural Brazilian place.
steps: Write the form of ir.
Put the pronoun after it.
Add the infinitive, unchanged.

examples.en: I am going to call you tomorrow.
She is going to help me.

watch: Te vou ligar sounds stiff in Brazil.
Vou ligar para você means the same and is also common.

sections.title: Fixed plans in the plain present
sections.text: For timetables and firm arrangements, Brazilians also use the simple present with a time word, just as English does with I leave tomorrow.
watch: When in doubt, use ir + infinitive: it is always right for plans.

exercises.hint: Take the nós form of ir, then add falar unchanged.
exercises.feedback: Nós takes vamos; the infinitive follows as it is.
exercises.explanation: Nós vamos falar: vamos (ir) + falar (infinitive). It means we are going to speak.

mistakes.why: Vão is the form for eles, elas and vocês, several other people. Nós includes the speaker and has its own form.
Only ir changes for the person. The second verb stays in the infinitive, ending in -r.
Vai is the singular form for ele, ela, você and a gente. Nós needs the plural form of ir.

exercises.hint: Eu has a short form of ir of its own.
exercises.feedback: Eu takes vou, followed by the infinitive.

mistakes.why: Vai is the form for ele, ela and você. Eu has its own form of ir.

exercises.hint: Eles is several people being talked about.
exercises.feedback: Eles takes vão, then the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Eles vão viajar: vão + viajar. They are going to travel.

mistakes.why: Vai is singular, for one person. Eles is plural and needs the plural form of ir.
Vamos is the nós form, a group that includes the speaker. Eles are other people.
Viajam is already conjugated. After ir, keep the infinitive in -r.

exercises.hint: Você takes the same verb form as ele and ela.
exercises.feedback: Você uses the third-person singular of ir.
exercises.explanation: Você vai trabalhar: vai + trabalhar. You are going to work.

mistakes.why: Vou is the eu form. Você is grammatically like ele or ela.
Vais goes with tu, which most of Brazil does not use with this form. Você takes the ele/ela form.
Vão is plural, for vocês or eles. Você is one person.

exercises.source: ver · a gente · futuro com ir
exercises.hint: A gente means we, but its verb is singular.
exercises.feedback: A gente takes the ele/ela form of ir.
exercises.explanation: A gente vai ver: a gente works like ela, so it takes vai. It means we are going to see.

mistakes.why: Vamos goes with nós. A gente means the same thing, but grammatically it is singular, like ela.
Vão is the plural form for eles and vocês. A gente takes a singular verb.

exercises.hint: Eles is several people being talked about.
exercises.feedback: Plural eles takes the plural form of ir.
exercises.explanation: Eles vão jantar em casa hoje: they are going to have dinner at home today.

mistakes.why: Vai is singular, for ele, ela, você or a gente. Eles is several people.
Vamos is the nós form and includes the speaker.
Vou belongs to eu only.

exercises.hint: The eu form of ir is short and irregular.
exercises.feedback: Eu takes vou.
exercises.explanation: Eu vou comprar pão: I am going to buy bread.

mistakes.why: Vai is for ele, ela and você, not for the speaker.
Ir is the infinitive. The first verb must change for eu; only the second stays unchanged.
Vamos is the nós form, several people.

exercises.hint: Você takes the same form as ela.
exercises.feedback: Você uses the ele/ela form of ir.
exercises.explanation: Você vai estudar hoje à noite? Are you going to study tonight?

mistakes.why: Vou is the eu form: it would mean the speaker.
Vão is plural, for vocês or eles. Você is one person.

exercises.source: They are going to eat at home.
exercises.hint: They is eles (or elas for women only). Pick the matching form of ir.
exercises.feedback: Eles takes vão, then comer.
exercises.explanation: Eles vão comer em casa: vão + comer. Elas is right for a group of women only.

mistakes.why: Vai is singular. They is several people and needs the plural form.
Comem is conjugated. After ir the verb stays in the infinitive.
Na casa means in the house of someone; at home is em casa, without the article.

exercises.hint: Vamos already shows who and when. What form does the second verb take?
exercises.feedback: After ir, the second verb is always the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Nós vamos jogar futebol no sábado: only ir changes for nós; jogar stays as it is.

mistakes.why: Jogamos is conjugated for nós. In this future only ir is conjugated; the second verb stays in its dictionary form.
Jogo is the eu form, and the second verb is never conjugated here anyway.

exercises.hint: Vai has done the work of showing the person.
exercises.feedback: The verb after ir stays in the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Ela vai trabalhar amanhã: she is going to work tomorrow.

mistakes.why: Trabalha is the ela form of the present. After vai, the verb does not change.
Trabalhou is a past form. The future with ir uses the infinitive.

exercises.hint: Two verbs in a row: only the first one changes.
exercises.feedback: Comem must go back to the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Eles vão comer pizza: vão carries the person, comer stays unchanged.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Both verbs are conjugated, but only ir should be.
Now the second verb is right but the first one is singular. Eles needs the plural form of ir.

exercises.hint: The -mos ending already sits on vamos.
exercises.feedback: Put estudar back in the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Nós vamos estudar hoje: we are going to study today.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The person is shown twice; the second verb must be the dictionary form.
That drops ir and changes the meaning to a plain present. Keep vamos and fix the second verb.

exercises.source: She is going to buy a car.
exercises.hint: One tile is conjugated, one is the infinitive. Which belongs after vai?
exercises.feedback: After vai, use the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Ela vai comprar um carro: vai + comprar.

mistakes.why: Compra is conjugated for ela. After ir the second verb stays in the infinitive.
That is the plain present, she buys a car. The sentence asks for going to.

exercises.hint: Put the eu form of ir first, then turn como back into its infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Eu como becomes eu vou comer.
exercises.explanation: Eu vou comer peixe: I am going to eat fish.

mistakes.why: Como keeps the eu ending. After ir, the verb goes back to the infinitive.
Vai is the ele/ela form. Eu needs its own form of ir.

exercises.source: You (plural) are going to see the film.
exercises.hint: Plural you is vocês, which takes the eles form of ir.
exercises.feedback: Vocês takes vão, then ver.
exercises.explanation: Vocês vão ver o filme: vão + ver.

mistakes.why: Veem is conjugated. After ir, keep the infinitive.
Vai is singular, for você. Vocês is plural.

exercises.hint: Where does não go: before or after the form of ir?
exercises.feedback: Não goes right before the conjugated verb.
exercises.explanation: Eu não vou trabalhar amanhã: I am not going to work tomorrow.

mistakes.why: Não never comes after the conjugated verb in this sentence. It goes in front of it.
The order is right, but vai is the ele/ela form. The subject is eu.

exercises.instruction: Make it negative: write não and ir.
exercises.hint: Two words: the negative word, then the ela form of ir.
exercises.feedback: Não comes first, then vai.
exercises.explanation: Ela não vai sair hoje à noite: she is not going to go out tonight.

mistakes.why: Não belongs in front of the verb, not after it.
The order is right, but vou is the eu form. The subject is ela.
That makes the sentence positive. The instruction asks for the negative.

exercises.hint: One word, placed before the form of ir.
exercises.feedback: Put não right before vamos.
exercises.explanation: Nós não vamos viajar: we are not going to travel.

mistakes.why: Não goes before the conjugated verb, not between ir and the infinitive.
In speech some Brazilians add a second não at the end, but never only at the end. The first one goes before the verb.

exercises.hint: Find the conjugated verb and put não before it.
exercises.feedback: Não moves in front of vou.
exercises.explanation: Eu não vou comer: I am not going to eat.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. Não sits after the conjugated verb.
The order is right now, but come is conjugated. Keep the infinitive.

exercises.source: He is not going to work tomorrow.
exercises.hint: Não, then the ele form of ir, then the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Ele não vai trabalhar.
exercises.explanation: Ele não vai trabalhar amanhã: não + vai + trabalhar.

mistakes.why: Não must come before the conjugated verb.
Trabalha is conjugated. After ir, keep the infinitive.

exercises.source: We are not going to watch TV.
exercises.hint: Não before the form of ir; then the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is conjugated and does not fit.

mistakes.why: Não goes before the conjugated verb.
Vemos is conjugated. After ir, use the infinitive.
That is the plain present, we do not watch TV. The sentence asks for going to.

exercises.instruction: Choose the time word that fits.
exercises.hint: Vou + infinitive talks about what is coming.
exercises.feedback: The future with ir needs a future time word.
exercises.explanation: Vou visitar minha mãe amanhã: I am going to visit my mother tomorrow.

mistakes.why: Ontem means yesterday. A plan with ir points forward, not back.

exercises.source: No sábado, eu ____ para a praia.
exercises.hint: Going somewhere needs ir only once.
exercises.feedback: Brazilians say vou para, not vou ir para.

mistakes.why: The first form of ir already means I am going. Adding ir again doubles the verb; Brazilians avoid it in careful speech and writing.

exercises.hint: Which word means towards a place?

exercises.explanation: Nós vamos para o cinema hoje: we are going to the cinema today.

mistakes.why: De means from or of. You go towards the cinema, not from it.
Com means with. A place you go to is introduced by another word.

exercises.source: Eles ____ (ir) para o Rio no domingo.

exercises.feedback: Eles vão para o Rio: ir alone says going there.
exercises.explanation: Eles vão para o Rio no domingo: they are going to Rio on Sunday.

mistakes.why: The form of ir already says they are going. Brazilians do not add the infinitive ir again.
Vai is singular. Eles is several people.

exercises.hint: You need the object form: call you.
exercises.feedback: The object pronoun te sits between vou and the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Eu vou te ligar amanhã: I am going to call you tomorrow.

Tu is a subject pronoun, the one doing the action. Here you are the person being called.

exercises.hint: In Brazil the pronoun leans on the infinitive.
